cells.Values and default: Copy of the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED`. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` compares the text with `true`. Any other text counts as not enabled. Unset: job `plan` always defines it. The value is empty when the repository variable is not defined. Empty counts as not enabled.
cells.Effect: Without the exact text `true`, `validate-invocation` stops a manual run that is not a dry run with `publishing refresh rollout is disabled`. It stops a scheduled run with `scheduled refresh rollout is disabled`. On a scheduled run, the job condition of `plan` tests the repository variable before this step runs. A dry run is a manual run with the workflow input `dry_run` set to `true`. The step passes the value as a command-line argument.

cells.Read by: Step conditions `env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` in the jobs `test-host` and `test-fpga` of both workflows, and in job `test` of `cmake-single-platform.yml` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
cells.Values and default: `true` or `false`. A workflow expression computes the text. The step conditions compare it with `true`. Unset: no default exists. Each job that reads it defines it in its `env` block.
cells.Effect: Steps with the condition `env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` run only when the value is `true`. The value is `false` on a first attempt when a test pass is already recorded for the same source and build. `cmake-single-platform.yml` computes it from `needs.build.outputs.artifact_verified`. `gcp-nix.yml` computes it from `needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required`. Both give `true` when `github.run_attempt` is above `1`. No script reads the name from the environment.

cells.Values and default: Whole number of seconds from `60` to `5400`, written with 2 to 5 digits. Other non-empty text stops the script with exit status 1. Unset: the measurement limit is 5400 seconds (90 minutes).
cells.Effect: Replaces the limit of 5400 seconds that `run-measurement` gives to the `bin/slice submit` measurement command through `timeout`. The workflow sets it from the input `measurement_timeout_seconds`. Job `plan` accepts a non-empty input only for a manual dry run (workflow input `dry_run` is `true`). A scheduled run has no input. `SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC` can then shorten the 5400 seconds.

cells.Values and default: Time of day in UTC, written `HH:MM:SS`. The workflow sets `06:30:00`. The script passes the text to `date -u -d` and does not check it. Unset: `06:30:00` UTC.
cells.Effect: On a scheduled run, the measurement limit is at most the time left until this time on the same UTC day, minus 30 seconds. A limit below 60 seconds stops the script. The script reads it only when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` is `schedule`. The 30 seconds are the wait of the `timeout` command between the TERM signal and the KILL signal. The stop message is `refresh deadline leaves less than 60 seconds for measurement`, with exit status 1.

cells.Read by: The step `Validate refresh invocation` of job `plan` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
cells.Values and default: Empty, or digits only: a whole number from `60` to `5400` seconds. Job `plan` takes it from the workflow input `measurement_timeout_seconds`. The input default is empty. Unset: `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` receives an empty argument. It skips the timeout check.
cells.Effect: The step passes the value to `bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation`. A non-empty value passes only when the event is `workflow_dispatch` and the dry-run state is `true`. A value outside the range fails the step. This variable only validates the input. Job `refresh` reads the same input as `SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. That variable sets the timeout of the Slice cost measurement. Both error texts start with `measurement timeout override`.

cells.Read by: `ci-bundle-test-artifact.sh`, `ci-resolve-test-artifact.sh`, `ci-restore-test-artifact.sh`, `prepare_handoff.py`, and steps of `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` (`bin/ci/ci-bundle-test-artifact.sh`, `bin/ci/ci-resolve-test-artifact.sh`, `bin/ci/ci-restore-test-artifact.sh` and 2 more files)
cells.Set by: `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, and `bin/ci/test_build_test_stage.py` for a test. No other workflow sets it.
cells.Values and default: Absolute path of a directory. The helper `ci-shared-nfs.sh` rejects a relative path when a script writes under it. `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` sets `/scratch/tron-build`. Unset: the 4 scripts use `/scratch/tron-build`. Empty: the 3 shell scripts use `/scratch/tron-build`. `prepare_handoff.py` uses the current directory.
cells.Effect: The 3 shell scripts publish, select and restore test artifact archives under `<value>/<source hash>`. `prepare_handoff.py` looks there for the marker of passed tests (the empty file `nix-tests-<identity>.passed`). In `prepare_handoff.py`, the option `--sentinel-root` overrides the variable. `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml` passes the value as an argument to `test_runtime.py` and `ci-cleanup-build-artifacts.sh`. The cleanup script deletes old directories under it. `ci-bundle-artifact.sh`, `ci-run-benchmark.sh` and the step `Mark test artifact passed` use the fixed path `/scratch/tron-build`.

cells.Read by: Steps of the 7 workflows that set it (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, `.github/workflows/publish-deb.yml` and 4 more files)
cells.Values and default: Version text of `uv` (the Python dependency manager). Every workflow that sets it writes `0.9.5`. Unset: no default exists. The paths then lack the version directory, for example `/tools/uv//uv`.
cells.Effect: The steps build the program path `/tools/uv/<UV_VERSION>/uv` or the directory `/tools/uv/<UV_VERSION>` from it. They store the program path in `UV`, or they add the directory to `PATH`. The workflows do not install `uv`. They use the program that the runner has under `/tools/uv/<UV_VERSION>`. `bin/ci/lint-ci-pins.sh` fails when the YAML files under `.github` give different values. `.github/workflows/positron-dice-deb.yml` sets the variable at job level. The other 6 workflows set it at workflow level.

cells.Values and default: Path of a directory. The script uses the text unchanged. Unset: the script uses `RUNNER_TEMP`. Without `RUNNER_TEMP` it uses `TMPDIR`. Without `TMPDIR` it uses `/tmp`. An empty value counts as unset.
cells.Effect: It sets the root directory for the state of each background check (a slow check that the script runs in the background of a job). The state of one check is in `background-check-<NAME>`. When `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is set, the script first appends `background-checks-<run id>-<attempt>-<job>` to the root. `bin/ci/README.md` asks matrix jobs with a shared temporary directory to set separate roots.

cells.Values and default: Whole number of days, digits only. Other text stops the script with the message `BUILD_ARTIFACT_MAX_AGE_DAYS must be an integer` and exit status 2. Unset: 3 days. An empty value also gives 3 days.
cells.Effect: The script removes build artifact directories whose modification time is at least this many days old. It looks only at directories named with 7 lowercase hexadecimal characters, at most 2 levels below the artifact root. The artifact root is the first argument of the script (default `/scratch/tron-build`). With `0` the script removes directories of any age. Bash reads a leading `0` as octal: `010` means 8 days, and `08` is an arithmetic error.

cells.Set by: No file in the repository sets it.
cells.Values and default: Positive number (`10`, `0.5`) with an optional unit: `s` seconds, `m` minutes, `h` hours, `d` days. No unit means seconds. Zero or other text stops the program (exit status 2). Unset: `10s` (10 seconds). Empty: the program stops with an argument error and exit status 2.
cells.Effect: It is the time limit for each unmount command (`fusermount3` or `fusermount` with `-uz`) and for the final `rm -rf` of the cleaned directory. When a command reaches the limit, the cleanup fails. `bin/ci/ci-cleanup-fuse-mount.sh` starts the program. The option `--timeout` replaces the variable. The program then does not check the variable. At the limit the program sends `SIGTERM` and then `SIGKILL` to the command. `bin/slice` calls the same cleanup function with a fixed limit of 10 seconds.

hints.problem: The introduction says: "These are variables of scripts under `bin/ci`. Each has a default that the caller can replace." Two of the 12 rows do not fit. `TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS` is read by `ingest/build-model.py`, not by a script under `bin/ci`, and it has no default that a caller replaces. `CI_CLEANUP_FUSE_TIMEOUT_S` is read by `bin/fuse_cleanup.py`. The row `TRON_INGEST_LIBSTDCXX_PATH` has the same reader as `TRON_MODEL_CACHE_LEASE_FDS` and sits in 3.4. One of the two was placed by its reader and the other by its setter.

cells.Set by: No workflow sets it. `bin/ci/test-perfetto-capture.sh` sets it for two checks.
cells.Values and default: Number of seconds. The script passes the text unchanged to the `timeout` command as the time limit. The script does not check the text. Unset: 300 seconds.
cells.Effect: It limits the run time of `nix build .#perfetto-host-binaries` in `resolve-perfetto-bin-dir.sh` (the script that prints the Perfetto program directory). At the limit, `timeout` sends TERM, and KILL 30 seconds later if the build still runs. The script then prints a hint and exits with status 124 or 137. The script does not read it when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` is non-empty. When `nix build` fails before the limit, the script exits with the status of `nix build`.

cells.Set by: No file in the repository sets it. A person who runs `bin/ci/bench_refresh.py` by hand can set it.
cells.Values and default: Any text. The script does not parse it. Unset: the `bitfile` row shows `<not provided>`. Empty: the row shows empty text.
cells.Effect: Sets the `bitfile` row of the Markdown summary that the script writes to the `--summary` file. The script reads it only when the option `--bitfile-metadata` is absent. The Slice cost-data refresh does not use it. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh` always passes `--bitfile-metadata`. The row then shows the bitfile identity and the device count from that JSON file. The manual procedure in `doc/slice.md` passes the option too.
